narrativeReportMd:
# MedicinalProductPackaged R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking changes found. R4 `MedicinalProductPackaged` is absent in R6 and the likely successor, `PackagedProductDefinition`, has a redesigned local content model.

## Scope
Compared local R4 resource elements to local R6 successor elements; excluded inherited base-artifact changes.

## Main migration themes
Resource identity replacement, package tree normalization, reference target renames, authorization externalization, batch identifier loss risk, and R6-only modifier/status semantics.

## Highest-impact findings
The root resource replacement, `packageItem`→`packaging` reshape, `Quantity`→`integer` package quantity, merged contained-item model, removed `marketingAuthorization`, and removed `batchIdentifier` are the main migration blockers.

## Follow-up analysis
Review companion resource conversions for `MedicinalProductDefinition`, `ManufacturedItemDefinition`, and `RegulatedAuthorization`, plus any official narrative/conversion guidance if available.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `MedicinalProductPackaged` is not present as an R6 resource; migration to `PackagedProductDefinition` is a hard instance-breaking conversion. Top concerns are resource identity, package tree reshape, removed authorization/batch fields, contained-item remodeling, and R6-to-R4 representability gaps.
summary.migrationThemesMd: A safe migration must rename the resource, map `subject` to `packageFor`, rebuild `packageItem` as `packaging`, convert package quantities and contained items, externalize marketing authorization, and preserve or review batch identifiers.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for StructureDefinition deltas and successor identity, but medium for exact business-intent mappings because no official ConceptMap, narrative page, or terminology expansions were supplied.

findings.title: R4 MedicinalProductPackaged is absent in R6 and replaced by PackagedProductDefinition

newState.summary: No same-name R6 StructureDefinition exists; PackagedProductDefinition is the likely successor.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 defines `PackagedProductDefinition` with similar package/container scope and retained packaging concepts.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The successor match is based on name, BRR/category metadata, description, local element overlap, and IDMP mappings.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Strict R6 parsers and REST routers will reject `resourceType: MedicinalProductPackaged`; R6 instances likewise require an explicit R6-to-R4 resource-type conversion.

justification.inferredGoal: Align package modeling with the R6 medicinal-product definition family.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the MedicinalProductPackaged resource identity in R6 with broadened definitions, or keep it as a deprecated base resource instead of replacing every resourceType.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of aligning and broadening packaged-product modeling is reasonable, but changing the base resource identity invalidates every R4 instance, profile URL, endpoint, generated class, and FHIRPath rooted at `MedicinalProductPackaged`. The evidence does not show that the R6 goal required a new wire-level resource type rather than carrying the old identity forward with clearer semantics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained `MedicinalProductPackaged` as the R6 resource and updated its definition to cover the broader medically related package scope, adding the R6 content model there. If `PackagedProductDefinition` was also introduced, the old resource could be deprecated for transition, but that would create duplicate resource identities for the same concept. Retaining the old name has a real naming-consistency cost, but it would preserve most existing R4 instances at the root level.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The legacy name would be less consistent with the R6 Definition family and broader packaged-item scope; defining both resource types would duplicate the same domain.

findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid `MedicinalProductPackaged` JSON is not R6-valid. R6 `PackagedProductDefinition` JSON is not R4-valid. This is a hard validation and runtime dispatch break, not just a semantic difference.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Convert resource type and canonical references first, then apply element-level transforms. Update generated models, endpoints, profile URLs, search names, and fixtures.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the `subject` element name and clarify it as the product this package is for, with updated or broadened target guidance instead of a same-purpose rename to `packageFor`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The relationship itself survived with the same cardinality and essentially the same meaning. Renaming `subject` to the clearer `packageFor` and following the MedicinalProduct-to-MedicinalProductDefinition transition improves readability, but it is not clearly necessary to accomplish the R6 modeling goal.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `subject` as the normative element, updated its definition to match the R6 wording, and adjusted target-profile guidance as part of the broader product-definition transition. If `packageFor` were added as a new synonym, the model would need precedence and consistency rules, so the cleaner alternative is simply living with the older but serviceable name.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The old `subject` name is less explicit, and target-resource migration still depends on the companion product resource transition; allowing both `subject` and `packageFor` would duplicate the same relationship.

findings.title: `legalStatusOfSupply` changed from CodeableConcept to repeatable jurisdiction-scoped backbone

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by element meaning, definitions, and nearby content model.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 CodeableConcept object cannot be copied to the R6 backbone array. R6 can express multiple jurisdiction-specific legal statuses that one R4 CodeableConcept cannot preserve.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent legal supply status per jurisdiction.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the old scalar `legalStatusOfSupply` for an unknown or default jurisdiction and add a separate jurisdiction-scoped repeatable element for multi-jurisdiction statuses.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Representing legal supply status per jurisdiction is a reasonable R6 goal, and the R6 backbone directly models the code/jurisdiction pair. A less-breaking design exists, but it would either be incomplete for multi-jurisdiction content or would introduce duplicate representations whose precedence and synchronization could affect regulatory interpretation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base alternative would retain `legalStatusOfSupply` as the legacy default status and add a new repeatable jurisdiction-scoped element. That would keep R4 instances valid and support the new use case, but implementations would need rules for whether the legacy value is equivalent to an entry with unknown jurisdiction and what happens when both forms are populated.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves common R4 data but creates two same-resource places for legal supply status; the old 0..1 CodeableConcept cannot represent multiple jurisdiction-specific statuses without ambiguity.

examples.examplesMd: No complete instance example is included; impact is derived from StructureDefinition element definitions.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 makes legal supply status richer by pairing codes with jurisdictions, but the JSON shape changes from a coded value to repeatable objects.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `legalStatusOfSupply.coding` directly under the resource are R6-invalid. R6 multiple jurisdiction entries are not cleanly R4-representable.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap an R4 value as `legalStatusOfSupply[0].code`; populate jurisdiction only if known. Use extensions or manual review for multiple R6 jurisdictions when mapping back.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition would have required keeping the old resource/element shape or publishing a normative conversion map. That would lower migration cost but preserve duplicated or ambiguous representations during the transition.

findings.title: Direct `marketingAuthorization` reference was removed from the package resource

newState.summary: No direct PackagedProductDefinition element; R6 RegulatedAuthorization.subject can target PackagedProductDefinition.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: No same-name local element exists; related R6 authorization resource supports package subjects.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old instances carrying `marketingAuthorization` are invalid in R6, and R6-to-R4 conversion must discover related RegulatedAuthorization resources or lose the link.

justification.inferredGoal: Generalize authorizations as separate regulated authorization resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain a deprecated direct `marketingAuthorization` link, possibly retargeted to RegulatedAuthorization, while also supporting the external `RegulatedAuthorization.subject` relationship.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Generalizing authorizations into `RegulatedAuthorization` is a reasonable modeling goal, especially because the R6 subject can cover many regulated artifacts. Keeping a local package field would reduce migration breakage but would undermine normalization unless it were only a deprecated mirror with strict consistency expectations.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `marketingAuthorization` on the package resource as an optional deprecated reference, either to the R6 authorization resource or as a compatibility bridge. This would preserve R4-shaped packages, but it would leave two authoritative paths for the same relationship and make bundle/server consistency checks necessary.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The direct and inverse authorization relationships could conflict; external authorization resources can carry broader subjects and metadata that a local shortcut cannot fully represent.

findings.title: `batchIdentifier` has no local PackagedProductDefinition successor

oldState.summary: 0..* BackboneElement with required `outerPackaging` Identifier and optional `immediatePackaging` Identifier.

newState.summary: No local batchIdentifier, outerPackaging, or immediatePackaging element was found on PackagedProductDefinition.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by element meaning, definitions, and nearby content model.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 batch numbering cannot be represented by a same-purpose local R6 field. Mapping it to a generic identifier may change semantics and dropping it can affect traceability.

justification.inferredGoal: Possibly separate batch-instance data from package-definition data.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `batchIdentifier` as a deprecated local element, or provide an explicit R6 batch/lot relationship before removing the local structure.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating batch-instance data from package-definition data may be a sound goal, but the available StructureDefinition evidence shows no local R6 successor for the outer/immediate packaging identifiers. Because these identifiers can be important for traceability, removing them without an evident base replacement is not clearly justified on the supplied evidence.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained the repeatable `batchIdentifier` backbone as deprecated while R6 introduced or documented the proper batch/lot artifact and relationship. That alternative is only partial because it preserves a concept that may not belong on a definition resource and could perpetuate mixed definition-versus-instance semantics.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Retaining it preserves traceability but continues carrying batch-instance identifiers on a package definition and may conflict with a cleaner separate batch/lot model; no same-purpose R6 base field was found.

findings.title: Required repeating `packageItem` became optional single `packaging` tree

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by element meaning, definitions, and nearby content model.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The old `packageItem` array is invalid in R6. Multiple R4 top-level package items cannot be copied into the single R6 top-level packaging field without hierarchy rules or splitting.

justification.inferredGoal: Normalize package contents into one packaging tree.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the recursive `packageItem` backbone, or accept both `packageItem` and `packaging` during transition while recommending a single primary packaging tree.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Normalizing the package into one packaging tree is a reasonable R6 goal, and the R6 definition explicitly distinguishes packaging containers/components from contained medically related items. The less-breaking alternatives preserve old instances but materially weaken the single-root model and require policy for multiple top-level R4 package items.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial alternative would keep `packageItem` as the recursive base element and clarify that one item is the primary root, or add `packaging` while retaining `packageItem` as deprecated. Either approach would avoid immediate invalidation of R4 data, but it would create duplicate tree shapes or leave the R4 multi-root pattern in the base model indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserving 1..* top-level package items undermines the single-root packaging model and leaves ambiguous handling for multiple roots; accepting both paths duplicates recursive structures.

evidence.detail: R6 nested packaging recurses via contentReference.

examples.examplesMd: No complete instance example is included; impact is derived from StructureDefinition element definitions.

findings.narrativeMd: The central packaging backbone was renamed and reshaped. This affects serializers, FHIRPath, generated accessors, recursive traversal, and validation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 data with `packageItem` is R6-invalid. R6 can omit packaging, which cannot satisfy the R4 required package item when converting back.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map one primary R4 package item to `packaging`; map nested package items to `packaging.packaging`. Define policy for multiple top-level R4 package items.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition would have required keeping the old resource/element shape or publishing a normative conversion map. That would lower migration cost but preserve duplicated or ambiguous representations during the transition.

findings.title: `packageItem.quantity` changed from required Quantity to optional integer

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by element meaning, definitions, and nearby content model.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The JSON shape changes from a Quantity object to an integer primitive. Unit-bearing, decimal, comparator, or missing R4 quantities need policy decisions.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate package-layer counts from contained-item amounts.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the packaging quantity as `Quantity` and constrain or recommend whole-number count semantics, while using `containedItem.amount` for item amounts.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R4 definition already described package quantity as the count of packages at the current layer, with the outermost always 1. Replacing a required `Quantity` object with an optional integer is a hard serialization and codegen break that does not appear necessary to separate package-layer counts from contained-item amounts.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `packaging.quantity` as `Quantity` with a narrowed definition, best-practice invariant, or profile guidance requiring whole-number count usage for package layers. `containedItem.amount` could still carry item quantities such as tablets or milliliters. The tradeoff is weaker base-level enforcement of integer-only counts, but that is a moderate validation cost rather than a need for a breaking datatype replacement.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping `Quantity` permits broader forms than a pure integer and needs guidance for units, decimals, and comparators, but it preserves old JSON and avoids duplicate same-fact fields.

evidence.detail: R6 uses Quantity for contained item amount.

examples.examplesMd: No complete instance example is included; impact is derived from StructureDefinition element definitions.

findings.narrativeMd: Package quantity has a direct codegen and serialization break: object-valued `Quantity` becomes primitive integer.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 Quantity JSON is invalid for R6 `integer`. R6 omitted quantity cannot satisfy R4 required quantity if reconstructing R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Convert only whole-number package counts to integer. Preserve or review units/comparators; use `containedItem.amount` for actual item quantity when appropriate.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition would have required keeping the old resource/element shape or publishing a normative conversion map. That would lower migration cost but preserve duplicated or ambiguous representations during the transition.

findings.title: Separate `device` and `manufacturedItem` arrays merged into `containedItem.item` CodeableReference

oldState.summary: Separate 0..* Reference arrays for DeviceDefinition and MedicinalProductManufactured.

newState.summary: Repeatable containedItem backbone with required CodeableReference item and optional amount.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by element meaning, definitions, and nearby content model.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old direct arrays are invalid in R6; target resources and datatype changed. R6 can contain concepts and additional resource types that R4 cannot represent.

justification.inferredGoal: Unify package contents and support broader medically related item types.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the old `device` and `manufacturedItem` arrays while adding a unified `containedItem` CodeableReference path for new item categories and concept-only entries.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Unifying contained package items and allowing broader medically related targets is a reasonable R6 goal. A compatibility design could preserve common R4 arrays, but it would not give R6 one canonical representation and would require implementations to merge or reconcile old arrays with the new CodeableReference model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial less-breaking base design would retain `device` and `manufacturedItem` as deprecated child arrays and add `containedItem.item` for the broader R6 set. This would preserve R4 instances for devices and manufactured items, but new targets such as packaged products, biologically derived products, nutrition products, and concept-only entries would still need the new path, creating long-term duplicate content channels.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Old arrays cover only two R4 target classes and duplicate the new canonical path; conflicting or redundant representations could persist indefinitely.

findings.title: R6 adds optional modifier element `status`

oldState.summary: No local R4 package lifecycle status modifier.

newState.summary: 0..1 CodeableConcept; isModifier=true; preferred binding to publication-status.

flags.isModifierReason: status can indicate that a record should not be treated as valid

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by element meaning, definitions, and nearby content model.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The optional addition does not invalidate R4 content, but R6 processors must not ignore a modifier status, and R4 has no local equivalent for reverse conversion.

justification.inferredGoal: Expose lifecycle validity directly on the package definition.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No R4-to-R6 base-design alternative is needed because `status` is optional additive R6 content and absent R4 instances remain valid after resource/element conversion.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding a lifecycle status that can indicate a record should not be treated as valid is reasonable for an R6 definition resource. This finding is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue in the calibration sense because the new modifier is optional and does not invalidate R4 content by its absence.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Not applicable. The compatibility concern is not preserving an R4 field in the R6 base design; it is that R6 processors must not ignore the new modifier and R6-to-R4 conversion cannot represent it locally without an extension or sidecar.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The remaining cost is runtime and R6-to-R4 handling: R6 consumers must process the modifier, and R4 conversion needs an extension or sidecar if status is present.
